That is a threat and intimidation directed at the passenger, and it is recorded in the in-app chat itself, so no statement-versus-record conflict arises: the chat record is complete and every message timestamped (F5). [F3 F4 F5] [SAFE-1]
C2: The driver's own written statement confirms the substance of the rider's account rather than contradicting it: he admits the rider tried to open the door and that he "told her to sit down ... and drove on" (F6). A driver who drives on while the passenger is asking to get out, after warning that he would lock the doors, leaves the rider unable to exit — the rider's stated fear for the ride (complaint) is consistent with F3/F4/F6. [F4 F6] [SAFE-1]
C3: Because a threat/intimidation message appears in the chat record (F4), the case must not be decided automatically: it goes to a person, with a fact summary, per SAFE-1. The rider's own record raises no credibility problem — 619 days on the platform, 4.8 rating, zero disputes and zero upheld in 90 days (F7) — while the driver carries 1038 trips in 90 days (F8), which is context for the human reviewer, not the basis of the finding. [F4 F7 F8] [SAFE-1]

[F7 F8] [SAFE-1]

events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.85)
events.body:
Factual summary for the human reviewer. This is a completed RydeX fixed-fare trip (Clarke Quay → Bedok Mall, pickup 17:08, drop-off 17:31, $32.86 fixed) with a complete, fully timestamped two-message chat record [F5]. At 17:09 the rider wrote "Please stop the car, I want to get out here" [F3]; one minute later, at 17:10, the driver wrote "Sit down or I lock the doors" [F4]. The driver's post-trip statement adds that the rider tried to open the door at the lights and that he told her to sit down "for her own safety" and drove on [F6]. The rider's complaint is that the driver threatened to lock her in and that she felt unsafe for the whole ride. The words of [F4] are a conditional statement by the driver made after the rider asked to exit, and [F6] is the driver's own admission that he continued driving rather than stopping; both are on the record and both sides agree the words must be read by a person. The SAFE-1 screen is therefore triggered — a threat/intimidation allegation appears in the record and is not mine to settle — so the case goes to a person without an automatic ruling [F3][F4][F6][SAFE-1].

The route and fare side is settled and yields nothing. GPS shows 15.4 km driven against a 15.5 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -0%) [F1], so there is no off-route segment and no RD-1 deviation to record; duration 23.7 min against a 21.8 min estimate [F2] is not an abnormal delay. The fare is a fixed RydeX quote of $32.86 [F1] and no fare or ERP facts exist, so no unpublished add-on can be identified and no amount is computable under FARE-1 or RD-2 [F1][FARE-1][RD-1].

On the safety screen specifically: I read the only two chat messages [F3][F4], the driver's statement [F6] and the rider's complaint. [F4] is hostile and aimed at the passenger at the moment she asked to leave, and it is capable of being read as conditioning her freedom to exit on her compliance; [F3] is a request to stop, not a threat; nothing in [F6] or the complaint alleges violence, sexual remarks or dangerous driving. My finding is "suspected": the words need a human reader, which is what SAFE-1 and the trace require, and the safety outcome is not for this adjudication [F4][F6][SAFE-1].

Profiles do not decide this. The rider's 619-day, 4.8-rated account with zero disputes in 90 days [F7] and the driver's 893 days, 1038 trips in 90 days, rating 4.62, zero disputes and zero upheld [F8] are context only, and neither can establish or defeat the safety allegation on its own [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. No account flag is issued here: RD-6 is not satisfied because no refund is due and no RD-1 violation is recorded, and its profile trigger (route_disputes_upheld_90d ≥ 1) is not met (0 upheld) [F8][RD-6]. If the human reviewer finds the message to be intimidation of the passenger, Ryde's code of conduct bar on abuse of any kind and its account-review mechanisms are for that reviewer to apply [F8][SAFE-1].

Because the safety screen is "suspected" this case must not be auto-decided; evidence_status is recorded as sufficient for the escalation only — the record contains the two timestamped messages and the driver's statement that the reviewer needs, and the safety outcome itself is deliberately left to a person.

ruling.recommended_action: Refer to a human reviewer under SAFE-1: read F3/F4 together with the driver's post-trip statement F6, treat the complaint's "whole ride" framing as unsupported, and decide whether the driver's words and his decision to drive on after a mid-ride request to exit warrant account action; contact the rider for a statement (timing of the door attempt, whether the doors were locked, where the vehicle was). Do not issue an automatic refund.

claims.assertion: The rider asked to be let out mid-ride — "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." (F3, 17:09) — and the driver's reply was "Sit down or I lock the doors." (F4, 17:10), i.e. the driver threatened to confine the rider in the vehicle when she asked to exit. That is a threat and intimidation directed at the passenger, and it is recorded in the in-app chat itself, so no statement-versus-record conflict arises: the chat record is complete and every message timestamped (F5).

The driver's own written statement confirms the substance of the rider's account rather than contradicting it: he admits the rider tried to open the door and that he "told her to sit down ... and drove on" (F6). A driver who drives on while the passenger is asking to get out, after warning that he would lock the doors, leaves the rider unable to exit — the rider's stated fear for the ride (complaint) is consistent with F3/F4/F6.

Because a threat/intimidation message appears in the chat record (F4), the case must not be decided automatically: it goes to a person, with a fact summary, per SAFE-1. The rider's own record raises no credibility problem — 619 days on the platform, 4.8 rating, zero disputes and zero upheld in 90 days (F7) — while the driver carries 1038 trips in 90 days (F8), which is context for the human reviewer, not the basis of the finding.

Any account action against the driver must come from the human review that SAFE-1 mandates and, on the profile side, can only be an additional request — the driver's clean 90-day dispute record (F8, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) is not itself a chargeable violation, and profile facts may never decide the case alone.

The detour/fare side of the trip does not support a separate money claim: the driver actually drove 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (F1) and the trip took 23.7 min against a 21.8 min estimate (F2); there is no off-route segment and no fare fact for this case, so the rider's remedy here rests on the safety escalation, not on a route refund.

weaknesses: The only direct evidence of the threat is the driver's one-line chat message F4; it contains no physical contact, no violence and no explicit threat of harm, and the driver's statement F6 recasts the same exchange as a safety instruction ("for her own safety") — the judge may read F4 as ambiguous rather than as intimidation, even though SAFE-1 requires the reading of the words to be made by a human.

The rider's own message F3 asks to stop at traffic lights on a 15.5 km express-type trip (F1/F2) and the driver's account in F6 says she tried to open the door; the other side will argue she created the danger, and there is no chat message showing she repeated the request or that the doors were in fact locked.
No medical, police or third-party record is in the fact table, so nothing corroborates the rider's subjective "felt unsafe for the whole ride"; the safety outcome depends entirely on F3/F4/F6.

The case yields no quantifiable refund: with 15.4 km driven vs 15.5 km optimal (F1) and no fare facts, I cannot ask for a fare reduction, so SAFE-1's escalate is the only remedy available and its result will be decided by a human, not by this adjudication.

claims.assertion: The trip was completed on the shortest and most direct route: GPS shows actual distance 15.4 km against an optimal route of 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -0%), so there is no off-route segment and no route-deviation violation to record.
There is no billing excess to refund: the ride was a fixed-price RydeX trip of $32.86 with no fare facts showing any unbilled or unpublished add-on, so no refund is computable under the fare rules.

The rider's own message at 17:09 ('Please stop the car, I want to get out here', F3) shows the dispute arose mid-journey over stopping, and the driver's reply at 17:10 ('Sit down or I lock the doors', F4) is one message on an otherwise complete, fully timestamped two-message record (F5) — there is no course of threatening or harassing conduct by the driver.

The driver's written statement that he told the rider to sit down for her own safety because she tried to open the door at the lights (F6) is consistent with the chat words 'Sit down' and with a stopped-in-traffic situation, and it dates the exchange to the start of the ride, not 'the whole ride' as the complaint claims.

The driver's record supports his account: 893 days on the platform, 1038 trips in 90 days, rating 4.62 and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (F8), so this is not a pattern of abusive conduct; the rider likewise has zero disputes (F7).

The word 'lock' used by the driver (F4) is, read in context, a safety instruction during a moving trip, not a threat, intimidation or harassment; but because the complaint alleges he 'threatened' the rider, the case should be screened and referred to a human reviewer rather than auto-decided, with the driver's offer to give a full account.

weaknesses: The driver's own words are on record and are the rider's best evidence: F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors') can be read as a threat or as an instruction that the rider was not free to leave, and the judge reads the words, not the driver's intent.

The driver's explanation that the rider 'tried to open the door at the lights' appears only in his post-trip statement F6; there is no GPS or timeline fact confirming a stopped vehicle or an open door, so the safety rationale rests on a statement rather than a system record.

The rider's message F3 is a direct request to be let out at 17:09, earlier than the 17:31 drop-off, and the driver did not stop; whether he was entitled to keep driving is not established by any fact in the table.

There are no fare, GPS corridor or traffic facts for this dispute type (fare and traffic tools returned empty), so the driver cannot show a system-recorded justification for the driving decision, and the complaint's 'whole ride' framing is rebutted only by inference from F2 and F6.

The rider's account is internally corroborated by her low-dispute, 4.8-rated profile (F7) and by the complete, timestamped two-message chat record (F5), so she cannot be dismissed as an unreliable complainant.

points.response: Conceded — the GPS shows 15.4 km driven against 15.5 km optimal (F1), so I make no route-deviation claim and my C5 already says the money side of this case fails.
Conceded — no fare facts exist for this dispute type, so no refund is computable; I withdraw any fare-based remedy and keep only the safety escalation.

SAFE-1 is not a 'pattern' test — it applies when a threat, intimidation or harassment appears in the chat, and a single message can be one: F4 records 'Sit down or I lock the doors' one minute after the rider asked to get out at 17:09 (F3), which is a conditional statement that she is not free to leave, and the point is precisely that a human must read it, not that it should be waved through.

The 'whole ride' framing is not a requirement of SAFE-1 and I do not rest on it: what matters is that the exchange is placed by the timestamps at 17:09–17:10 (F3, F4) while drop-off was 17:31, and the driver's own statement admits he told her to sit down and 'drove on' (F6) — driving on against her request is the continuation, and the 'at the lights' detail appears only in F6, a post-trip statement, with no GPS or timeline fact confirming a stopped vehicle.

The driver's clean 90-day record (F8, 0 disputes, 0 upheld) does not answer what he wrote in F4; and since profile facts may never decide the case, that same rule cuts against using the rider's 619-day, 4.8-rated, zero-dispute account (F7) to bolster the driver either.

We agree on the only operative point: F4 must be read by a person, which is exactly the escalate outcome SAFE-1 prescribes, and on a plain reading 'or I lock the doors' conditions the rider's freedom to exit on her compliance with an instruction — the words, not the driver's stated intent, are what the reviewer reads.

Accepted that F3 and F4 are on the record, but the move from those words to 'threat and intimidation' is the rider's interpretation, not a fact: F5 shows only two timestamped messages, and F4's actual words ('Sit down or I lock the doors') are an instruction during a moving trip, which SAFE-1 leaves the human reader to judge.

F6 does not confirm confinement: it says the rider tried to open the door at the lights and that the driver told her to sit down 'for her own safety' before driving on, and the trip completed normally (F1) — no fact shows the doors were locked or that she was prevented from exiting at the destination.
